newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to bring the Internet to its villages.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to bring the Internet to its villages.

text.p: Indonesia said on Monday it planned to start developing telecommunications facilities which could provide multimedia services, including the Internet, to all districts across its vast archipelago.

Jonathon Parapak, secretary-general of the Tourism, Post and Telecommunications Ministry, said the government hoped to start achieving its ambitious goal of making such technology accessible to more than 3,800 sub-districts within five years.

"Telecommunications facilities would be offered to make it possible for villagers across the country to use multimedia services, including the Internet, for education, leisure, medical and other things," Parapak told a news conference.
More than 80 percent of Indonesia's nearly 200 million people live in the nation's 65,000 villages spread across more than 13,000 islands.
Parapak said the government would ask state-owned telecommunications firm PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) and privately owned telecommunications firms to take part in the project.
He said the project was necessary to build the country's telecomunications for the 21st century. He did not give further details.
The Indonesian postal service has already set up its own internet service provider (ISP), Wasantara-Net, which can be accessed by local subscribers in all 27 provinces.
Computers are provided at many large post offices across the country as they are out of the financial reach of most people in Indonesia, where the average annual income is around $1,000.
Telkom said that as of September there were 3.92 million telephone lines in service in Indonesia.
